question: In Microsoft Word, where do I go to set my own page margins instead of using a preset?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Microsoft Word, to set your own page margins instead of using a preset, go to the Layout tab and select the Margins icon. From the drop-down menu, choose the Custom Margins option at the bottom. This will open a dialog box where you can adjust the margins to your desired measurements [3b0d5af459cdb898927e175429808f0a08c08fce01cb66e7b79cecb673be4a2e].

results.text: To adjust the margins of a page, go to the Layout tab. Select the Margins icon, and a drop-down menu will appear. The default margin is Normal (1 inch on all sides), but this can be adjusted via the prepopulated options, such as for different layouts with narrower margins. If you want to set your own margins, choose the Custom Margins option at the bottom of the drop-down menu. In the dialog box shown in Figure 3.7, notice how you can adjust the margins to be various measurements.

question: According to the Word layout guidance, which page orientation works best when a table or graph would not fit well on a vertical page?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: According to the Word layout guidance, the landscape orientation works best for documents with tables and graphs that would not fit well on a vertical page [c507bf8ca42f95992b2ceb8e356c17c99f22796ccac0f2ab03e489138bda50c7].

events.query: According to the Word layout guidance, which page orientation works best when a table or graph would not fit well on a vertical page?

results.text: Page orientation refers to whether the page is vertical or horizontal. The default in Word is the vertical layout, called portrait orientation. This layout works best for everyday text documents, such as business reports and correspondence. The horizontal layout is known as landscape orientation, and works best for documents with tables and graphs that otherwise would not fit well on a vertical page.

question: Why might a team use double-spacing in a working Word document while collaborators are using Track Changes?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: A team might use double-spacing in a working Word document while collaborators are using Track Changes because it allows for better visibility of the changes or edits. Double-spacing makes it easier to see the revisions in progress by providing a complete line of space between lines, which can be particularly useful when there are multiple collaborators involved in editing the document [afc2e7613c6d45baebd58d9f8d446cd1e038c9ce4b5f93c9f65aaaeb1f7d71f7].

In addition to single-and double-spacing, users can use 1.5-spacing, or set custom spacing between lines within a paragraph (Figure 3.16).

question: Why does the Word heading guidance advise against using color to indicate hierarchy levels?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: The Word heading guidance advises against using color to indicate hierarchy levels because it is neither logical nor accessible. Using color alone does not provide a clear rationale for why one level would be higher or lower than another. Additionally, relying on color can be problematic for users who are visually impaired or have other accessibility needs, as some colors may not be easily perceived by them [1ed4a54741e20e44698887612d3a2038c8cb8aa6295927c3314d441645e42131].

Different heading levels can be used to create a hierarchy of content that also helps users best understand the material. In Word, headings can be set using styles that give them additional functionality, such as quickly displaying an outline of your document and providing the ability to link to or between sections. You can also generate a table of contents using headings.

question: In Microsoft Word, how does resolving a comment differ from deleting it?

answer: In Microsoft Word, resolving a comment differs from deleting it in that deleting a comment removes it completely from the document, while resolving a comment retains the comment in a history stored digitally with the document. question: In Word, why should body text and headings be assigned styles before applying a document theme?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Word, body text and headings should be assigned styles before applying a document theme because styles act as codes that tell Word how to format various sections of the document. Without these style codes, the theme won't know how to apply itself to the document. By labeling or coding all the styles in the document, such as applying the Normal style to body text and Heading styles to headings, you enable the themes and styles to be used to their full capacity [a07ae04c1c78db52862e80dc7c83421ae6a546fcda8e2b64420d6c630cb9c137] [e11fe753c964b68626110940ca20426586a00a22c83354712341fbd0c41dde69].

question: In Google Docs, which paste option should I use to bring in text from a website without its original font, size or color?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Google Docs, to paste text from a website without its original font, size, or color, you should use the "Paste without formatting" option. This tool allows you to copy and paste text only, without any of the source formatting such as font, font size, or color [7cefc6559dc1c7d55384366a08b4599c7f984303df7e587f27f72e410c72a1f8].

results.text: On a Mac, these commands are Command+Z and Command+Y, respectively. Any time a Ctrl+ function is used on a Windows computer, the corresponding function key on a Mac will be the Command key. Paste without formatting is a useful tool for copying and pasting text only, without any of the source formatting (such as font, font size, or color). This is particularly helpful when copying and pasting from an email or website.

question: In Google Docs, how does applying heading styles affect the document outline as a heading hierarchy is built?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: In Google Docs, applying heading styles affects the document outline by adding the styled text to the outline pane on the left. As you apply styles within a hierarchy, the document outline reflects this hierarchy, making it easier to manage and navigate long documents. For example, when a heading style is applied to a section like "Industry and Market Analysis," it appears in the document outline as a heading, helping to organize the document's structure effectively [41f5fa309109c033cf289cc4d1503bd10f21695983db84b1e2645e2b25faba2b].

For example, you can see that “Industry and Market Analysis” is now listed on the outline as a heading. This can be particularly useful when managing long documents, which Document Preparation covers.

question: In Google Docs, I want to move an entire paragraph to the right rather than indent only its first line. Which command should I use?

config.context_selection: rank order, unique IDs, whole chunks only

answer: To move an entire paragraph to the right in Google Docs, you should click anywhere in the paragraph, go to the Format menu, hover over Align & indent, and select Increase indent [1e7219ea9c285d741230328de53c84a986ef96ad5c886bed03fe8d66e7438d66].

events.query: In Google Docs, I want to move an entire paragraph to the right rather than indent only its first line. Which command should I use?

results.text: To indent a body of text, the first line of the selection is indented to the right five spaces, which is the convention for indenting the first line of a paragraph. To do this indentation, press the Tab key on your keyboard. But if you want to move the entire paragraph to the right, click anywhere in the paragraph and go to the Format menu, then hover over Align & indent, and lastly, select Increase indent (Figure 3.47).

results.text: Docs also makes aligning and indenting text simple. As with modifying the line spacing, you can place your cursor anywhere on a single paragraph and adjust the alignment for the whole paragraph. You can either choose an indent from the action bar, or go to the Format menu, then hover over Align & indent, then choose how you want to align the paragraph. If you want to align many paragraphs, just select them all together with the mouse, and then follow the same steps.

results.text: When you share the market trends report with your colleagues for their input, you need to make sure that everyone’s individual edits are captured in a clear way, similar to Track Changes in Word. The way to do this is through Suggesting mode, as the chapter on Essentials of Software Applications for Business introduced. To turn on Suggesting mode, go to the top right of the Docs window and look for the drop-down menu that says Editing. As you click on it, select Suggesting, as Figure 3.62 shows.

results.text: Is Transparency Always the Right Choice? Suggesting mode in Docs and Track Changes in Word serve the same purpose: Both help teams collaborate and share documents. These functions also help teams maintain accountability on the document’s grammar, usage, style, guidelines, and subject matter inaccuracies or faults. Google automatically logs the chain of events of the addition or editing of text by time and collaborator, tracking who made each change and when they did it.
